gap.description: The SERP is dominated by indoor 'best/biggest' fight-gym branding (Dang) and out-of-town training resorts (Tiger, Santai, The Camp), plus editorial listicles that rank gyms by size/reputation. Almost none lead with a warm, FAMILY + OPEN-AIR positioning, and few combine fully transparent public pricing WITH a clear scannable schedule on the main classes page. Inclusivity is stated generically ('all levels welcome') but rarely owned as a brand promise for women, kids, nervous first-timers, and solo travelers. There is a clean opening for an in-/near-town camp that pairs honest published prices + a clear weekly timetable + a genuinely beginner-and-family-friendly, golden-hour garden vibe rather than the hardcore warrior-gym aesthetic.

weakness: Tiger / Santai / The Camp hide pricing behind a separate packages page
Top-ranked brands sell on 'biggest/best/hardest', not warmth or inclusivity
Generic 'all levels welcome' line with no real reassurance for women/kids/first-timers
Editorial listicles (topmuaythai, gymbangarang) capture the comparison query but offer no booking
Few pages present prices AND a clear weekly schedule together on one classes page
Open-air / garden / golden-hour experience essentially unrepresented on page-one gyms
recommended_angle: Position /classes as the transparent, beginner-and-family-friendly alternative: lead with fully public prices and a clean weekly schedule right on the page, framed around Wildcat's open-air garden, golden-hour camp where women, kids, and first-timers feel welcome — 'come for the fight, stay for the family' — instead of the biggest-gym/hardcore-fighter pitch the page-one competitors all repeat.
